---
title: "Glossary"
---

Terms used in the course, in alphabetical order. Each entry names the modules that use it.
Clinical terms are defined in plain words for engineers; they are not clinical guidance.

Ablation
: Destroying a small area of heart tissue on purpose, for example by radiofrequency heating, to stop an arrhythmia. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Action potential
: The rise and fall of the transmembrane voltage when a heart cell is excited. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Activation wavefront
: The moving boundary between excited and resting tissue. Also called the front. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Arrhythmia
: An abnormal heart rhythm. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Atrial fibrillation (AF)
: A fast, irregular rhythm of the upper chambers, without organized atrial activity. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Atrium (plural atria)
: One of the two upper chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Average precision (PR AUC)
: The area under the precision–recall curve, averaged over thresholds. Unlike the ROC AUC it falls when positives are rare. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Bipolar electrogram
: The difference between the signals of two nearby electrodes. It acts like a spatial derivative: it keeps local detail and rejects distant activity, but depends on the bipole's orientation to the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Clique
: A small group of electrodes, such as a triangle or a square, whose bipoles are combined to estimate the local electric field. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Conduction velocity
: The speed at which the activation wavefront travels through tissue, in m/s (1 m/s = 1 mm/ms). [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Cross-entropy
: The loss most classifiers minimize: minus the log of the probability given to the true class. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Data augmentation
: Training on altered copies of the data (for example, flipped or noisier signals) so a model ignores the alteration. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Dataset shift
: Any difference between the data a model was trained on and the data where it is used: in class mix (prior shift), in the recordings (covariate shift) or in what labels mean. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Decapolar catheter
: A catheter with ten electrodes along its shaft. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Dice coefficient
: Overlap of a predicted and a true region: twice the shared area over the sum of the two areas, from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (identical). [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Electrogram
: The voltage an electrode records from currents crossing cell membranes nearby. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Endocardium
: The inner surface of the heart wall. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

External validation
: Testing a frozen model on data from another place or time that played no part in training or tuning. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Far-field signal
: Activity that an electrode picks up from tissue that is not directly under it. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Federated learning
: Training one model across sites that keep their data; only model updates are shared. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Focal loss
: A cross-entropy that down-weights examples the model already gets right, so training attends to rare and hard ones. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Focal source
: A small region from which activation spreads outward. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Gaussian mixture model
: A probability model that describes data as a weighted sum of normal distributions; fitted with the EM algorithm to find clusters without labels. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Graph convolution
: A network layer that mixes each point's features with those of its neighbours on a graph, such as the vertices of a mapping mesh. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Implantable loop recorder (ILR)
: A small device placed under the skin that records the ECG for years and sends alerts when its detector fires. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Intrinsic deflection
: The steepest downstroke of a unipolar electrogram, used to mark local activation. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Leave-one-patient-out
: A test scheme that trains on all patients but one and tests on that one, in turn, so no patient is in both sets. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Local activation time
: The moment the activation wavefront reaches a given site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Low-voltage area
: A region whose bipolar voltage falls below a chosen cut-off. It is often read as scar, but the voltage also depends on the catheter and the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Myocardial infarction
: Death of an area of heart muscle caused by loss of its blood supply. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Omnipolar electrogram
: A signal built from a clique by estimating the local electric field and reading it along the direction of propagation, which removes most orientation dependence. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Pacing
: Stimulating the heart electrically from an electrode at a chosen site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Photoplethysmography (PPG)
: Measuring blood-volume changes in tissue with light; the basis of pulse sensing in watches and trackers. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Positive predictive value (PPV)
: The share of positive results (alerts, flags) that are truly positive; it depends on prevalence. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd), [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Premature beat
: A beat that comes earlier than expected, usually followed by a longer interval; a common cause of false AF alerts. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Receptive field
: The stretch of input that one output of a network depends on. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Remote monitoring
: Sending data from an implanted or wearable device to a clinic, where alerts are reviewed. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

RR interval
: The time between two successive R peaks of the ECG, one ventricular beat to the next. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Scar
: Fibrous tissue that has replaced heart muscle. It conducts poorly or not at all. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Sinus rhythm
: The normal heartbeat, started by the heart's own pacemaker. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Softmax
: The function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities that are positive and sum to one. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Spatial frequency
: How quickly a pattern varies in space, in rad/mm. Fine detail has high spatial frequency. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Transmembrane voltage
: The voltage across a cell membrane, inside minus outside. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Unipolar electrogram
: The signal of one electrode measured against a distant reference electrode. It sees local and far-field activity. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricle
: One of the two lower chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricular tachycardia
: A fast rhythm that starts in the ventricles. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Volume conductor
: The conducting medium (tissue and blood) through which currents spread from their sources to the electrodes. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)
